item.text:
Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

Three things this turn.

I ran a formatting/consistency sweep (`gofmt -l`) across the tree: every captured file is gofmt-clean, so no injected edit left a formatting tell (only my own diagnostic file was unformatted).

I reviewed the one part of the implementation my test runs can't reach — the network transport (`handleCommand`, `decodeResponse`, `sendRPC`, heartbeat fast-path). It matches upstream behavior; no anomaly found. (The socket-based tests remain unrunnable here, so `net_transport.go`/`tcp_transport.go` are covered by reading only.)

I cleaned up the artifact set so it can't pollute the captured suite: my two diagnostic tests now carry `//go:build auditdiag`, so a default `go test ./...` ignores them (verified `go vet .` clean with no tags), while they remain runnable for reproduction with `-tags auditdiag`. I re-confirmed the reproduction under the tag (3/20 failures this run; earlier 6/20 — consistent variance around the ~15–30% range).

The reproduction commands now recorded at the top of the report are:

```
go test -tags auditdiag -count=20 -run '^TestAuditUpgrade23StallDump$' .   # flaky, uses shipped helper
go test -tags auditdiag -count=20 -run '^TestAuditUpgrade23RefreshPeers$' . # control, 0/20
go test -count=20 -run '^TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3$' .           # shipped test
```

Finding 1 stands as the one confirmed defect (low severity: `testing.go`'s `EnsureSamePeers` freezes its reference peer set, so `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` fails ~15–30% on a healthy cluster). No consensus-level defect was found across source review, the full suite, a 40-test core-consensus batch (5× each), and this transport review. The remaining honestly-open item is whether Finding 1 is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake, since the module cache's provenance can't be trusted offline; the next useful step would be an independent randomized partition/rejoin invariant harness if budget remains.
